date_label: Close friends by 1892-93 (The Blackmailers, written together, produced June 1893); 'remained close friends for the rest of his life' (both died 1934); later years together in Edinburgh, where Raffalovich built St Peter's Church for Gray.
summary: Gray and Raffalovich were close by 1892-93, when they wrote The Blackmailers together (Prince of Wales's Theatre, June 1893) - the editors call Raffalovich Gray's 'close friend' and record the belief that he 'revenged himself' on Wilde by breaking up Wilde's friendship with Gray, 'with whom Raffalovich remained close friends for the rest of his life'. The bond ran unbroken to their deaths in the same year, 1934: Gray became a Roman Catholic priest, Raffalovich built St Peter's Church, Edinburgh, for him, and Gray's edition of Beardsley's last letters (1904) was of letters written to Raffalovich. The verified sources attest lifelong devotion without characterizing the bond sexually; the celibacy question is left open.
